html:
The Karen conflict is an armed struggle by the Karen National Union for self-rule in eastern Burma, which began in 1949 and continues today. It is often called the world's longest-running civil war.

Many Karen had become Christian under British rule and fought for Britain in the Second World War. They were left out of the Panglong Agreement and feared Burman rule. In 1949 Karen forces nearly took Rangoon.

The army's campaigns burned villages and drove hundreds of thousands of Karen into refugee camps in Thailand. A ceasefire in 2012 broke down after the 2021 coup, when Karen forces joined the wider revolt.
